title: Venture | VCs Bid Up AI Startup SPVs — Another Foam Signal?
summary: The VC secondary market’s SPV trade may itself be an AI bubble tell. Funds are buying more late-stage private shares of hot AI startups — increasingly via special purpose vehicles. Scarcity has made some SPVs sellable above the last primary/tender price — great for sellers,
author: Unique Research
html:
Unique Research · Insight / Special Report · August 29, 2024 · Source: TechCrunch reporting via Caplight / StepStone (compiled)

The VC secondary market’s SPV trade may itself be an AI bubble tell. Funds are buying more late-stage private shares of hot AI startups — increasingly via special purpose vehicles. Scarcity has made some SPVs sellable above the last primary/tender price — great for sellers, riskier for buyers.

How the structure works

Secondaries let employees or VCs who bought in primaries sell to new investors. Private companies control who holds stock, so many funds can’t buy direct. Those who can wrap shares in SPVs and sell interests to other VCs or accredited individuals. Buying an SPV interest ≠ owning company stock directly — Caplight co-founder/CEO Javier Avalos: you become an investor in another investor’s vehicle that controls some shares.

Some SPVs +30%

SPVs aren’t new; premium-priced SPV interests are the new tell. Avalos has seen Anthropic- or xAI-backed SPVs priced ~30% above the last round or tender. For institutions that already hold real shares: mark up the SPV and book ~30% profit immediately. For smaller VCs shut out of primaries, even expensive SPVs can be the only path to upside if the company wins.

Risks of owning the wrapper

  • Less financial visibility; no direct company–investor communications
  • No direct voting rights; no separately negotiated terms (pro-rata, IPO/M&A vetoes, etc.)
  • At a 30% premium, you need substantial further appreciation to get paid — and a take-private/M&A that works for voting holders can strand overpaying SPV LPs

StepStone partner Brian Borton (June, to TechCrunch): the classic secondary edge is buying below current marks. Buyers of rich AI SPVs know that — and are still betting companies outperform. With AI valuations high while apps/revenue still early, that is a large risk.

— END —
